title: The Evening Brief: A Sunday of finishes: Solheim, Rays, Garcia, and a stunner in Stillwater
dek: Championships closed in golf, boxing, and tennis semifinals while the NFL's Week 1 aftermath brought a coaching extension, a marquee injury, and a $37 million question on Lamar Jackson's future.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The day's common thread is closure arriving on multiple fronts at once: Europe reclaimed the Solheim Cup, the Rays clinched the first playoff spot of 2026, and Garcia and Rybakina defended or claimed titles, even as the NFL's Sunday news cycle stayed focused on what comes next for Garrett, Stribling, and Jackson.
bottom_line: Sunday closed several open questions at once: Europe reclaimed the Solheim Cup 15-13, Ryan Garcia stopped Conor Benn to retain his WBC welterweight title, Elena Rybakina won the US Open and the world No. 1 ranking, and the Rays became the first team to clinch a 2026 playoff spot. The NFL's parallel thread was less about results than about cost and commitment: the 49ers extended Kyle Shanahan while confirming rookie De'Zhaun Stribling's month-long absence, Myles Garrett heads to injured reserve for knee surgery, and Lamar Jackson's extension talks remain stalled entering the season. The reporting does not connect these threads causally; they share only the calendar. What to watch: today's US Open men's final between Shelton and Zverev and the FIBA Women's World Cup gold medal game, Stribling's and Garrett's medical updates in the coming weeks, and whether Jackson-Ravens talks resume after the season.
body: The single fact that anchors this Sunday is the Rays becoming the first team in 2026 to clinch a playoff berth, finishing off a 3-1 win over the Astros on September 12 on a Junior Caminero walk-off home run. That result sits alongside a string of other conclusions reached today: Europe beat the USA 15-13 to reclaim the Solheim Cup, Ryan Garcia stopped Conor Benn in the second round to retain his WBC welterweight title, and Elena Rybakina beat Aryna Sabalenka to win the US Open and claim the world No. 1 ranking. Across sports, today read as a day of decisions rendered, several of them decisively.

In golf, Europe's win at Bernardus Golf Club ended a drought dating to 2015, sealed when Lottie Woad beat Auston Kim on the 17th green after Carlota Ciganda's win over Jennifer Kupcho mathematically locked the outcome. The Americans had moments, Alison Lee's comeback from four holes down against Esther Henseleit among them, but Europe's Sunday singles performance held.

In boxing, Garcia improved to 26-2 by stopping Benn at 1:25 of the second round in Las Vegas, a fight that ended with Benn hospitalized as a precaution and Garcia turning his attention to Teofimo Lopez, who taunted him from ringside. Benn's future, including a possible weight-class move he had signaled regardless of Saturday's result, remains with him and Zuffa Boxing.

In tennis, Rybakina's 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 win over Sabalenka delivered her third career Grand Slam and left her one French Open title short of the career Grand Slam. Skupski and Harrison added the men's doubles title, their second major together after January's Australian Open. Ben Shelton's semifinal win over Frances Tiafoe sets up Sunday's men's final against Alexander Zverev, a match still to be played as of this writing, that would end a 23-year American men's Grand Slam drought if Shelton wins. Team USA's basketball team, fresh off a 76-66 semifinal win over Spain, plays France for the FIBA Women's World Cup gold medal today as well.

Football carried the day's roster and injury news. The Rams' Myles Garrett will undergo arthroscopic knee surgery and go on injured reserve, missing at least four games after recording zero tackles in 39 snaps in Week 1, with earliest eligibility to return in Week 6 against Arizona. Tight end money moved in both directions: the Packers signed Tucker Kraft to a four-year, $75 million extension, and the Raiders signed Michael Mayer to a three-year, $45 million deal, the largest three-year contract for a tight end in league history, while Mayer fills in for an injured Brock Bowers. Lamar Jackson, meanwhile, remains without a contract extension as the season begins, with ESPN reporting no substantive talks have taken place between Jackson and the Ravens.

On the field, the Bears' 59-37 win over the Panthers featured 291 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns on 39 carries, and the Lions survived a 21-0 lead evaporating into a 31-30 overtime win over the Saints after New Orleans' two-point conversion attempt failed with 1:34 left. Oklahoma State's 39-31 upset of No. 6 Oregon, as a 23.5-point underdog, snapped a 21-game losing streak and marked, per ESPN's reporting cited by CBS Sports, the first time in FBS history a team has snapped a 10-plus-game losing streak by beating a top-10 opponent. Contreras returned to the Red Sox lineup from the injured list, and MLB's Friday tributes marking the 25th anniversary of September 11 rounded out the day's institutional notes.

The stories do not point to a single driver behind these outcomes. Contract extensions for Shanahan, Kraft, and Mayer reflect franchises paying to lock in continuity and depth ahead of a season already underway; the injuries to Stribling and Garrett reflect the physical cost of that same Week 1; and Jackson's stalled talks reflect a player choosing to defer money conversations to focus on the season, per ESPN's reporting. None of the inputs offer a broader causal thread tying the football business moves to the on-field outcomes elsewhere in the day.
desk_boards were unavailable this run, so all scores and standings above come directly from the day's reported stories and carry their own datelines.

The week ahead brings concrete checkpoints. Shelton and Zverev play the US Open men's final today; Team USA and France play for the FIBA Women's World Cup gold medal today as well. The 49ers return to action on September 22, a date that may bring clarity on whether Stribling needs surgery. Garrett's earliest return is the Rams' Week 6 game against Arizona on September 28. The Rays' pursuit of the AL East title and a Wild Card Series bye continues with at least 16 more regular-season games. And Jackson's contract situation, per ESPN, is not expected to move again until after the season, against a reported $84.3 million cap commitment.
